title: STT packed-format manifest
description: Canonical schema for the per-dataset `manifest.json` of the STT packed format (formatVersion 2). This is the cross-language wire contract: the Rust writer (`crate::pack::Manifest`) and every reader (TS `@poopdeck.gl/core` `PackedManifest`, Rust `PackedReader`) MUST agree with this document. Unknown properties are permitted at every envelope level (additive evolution within a formatVersion): readers MUST ignore fields they do not recognize. See docs/spec/stt-packed-format.md.

allOf.$comment: formatVersion-1 manifests MUST NOT carry the `schemas` table (v2-only; the Rust reader rejects it).

formatVersion.description: Packed format version — the AUTHORITATIVE discriminator (stt-packed-format.md §5.2 authority rule): STTP/STTD object magic with object-absolute blob offsets, manifest-embedded `schemas` templates, and the sectioned layer frame. Distinct from the directory codec version (see `directory.directoryVersion`) and the tile-payload encoding. Readers MUST refuse values outside this enum at open.

schemas.description: formatVersion 2 ONLY (v1 manifests MUST NOT carry the key): the dataset's Arrow IPC schema templates, embedded (stt-packed-format.md §3.2). Each entry is the raw template bytes (stream start through the end of the Schema message) base64-encoded, addressed by their blake3-128 hash — the 16-byte reference v2 layer frames carry. Entries MUST be sorted by `hash` and deduped (byte-reproducible manifests). Readers MUST validate blake3_128(data) == hash for every entry at open, failing the whole dataset loudly on any mismatch, then resolve frame references against the resulting registry.

hash.description: blake3-128 of the raw (decoded) template bytes, 32 lowercase hex chars.

data.description: The raw template bytes, standard base64 (padded).

capabilities.description: OPTIONAL required-to-understand feature declarations (see stt-packed-format.md §3.1). Each entry names a feature the writer used that RE-TYPES existing tile columns, so a reader that does not implement it would silently misdecode; a reader MUST refuse a dataset declaring a capability outside the set it implements (loud failure at open). The current registry is the top-level `x-stt-capability-registry` array of this schema — the single machine-readable source both reference implementations pin their constants against in CI. Values are deliberately open-ended strings — future registry entries are added by spec revision (extending `x-stt-capability-registry`) without invalidating old manifests, and readers enforce their OWN implemented set, not this schema. Additive columns (triangles, vector groups, ...) never need a capability. Absent = none used (the shape of every pre-capabilities manifest; writers omit the key rather than emit an empty array).

compression.description: Per-blob compression codec. Every tile blob is compressed independently (no shared zstd dictionary), so a streaming reader can decode any blob in isolation. The format is zstd-only: `zstd` is the default and only real codec (it beats gzip on both ratio and browser-side decode speed, so no writer has ever emitted gzip), and `none` exists only for already-incompressible blobs. The canonical reader (Rust `PackedReader`) rejects any value outside this set.

blobOrdering.description: OPTIONAL. The concrete space-filling blob byte-ordering the writer resolved and laid down (`--blob-ordering`, see stt-packed-format.md §5). Informational: it records how the on-disk blob byte order was chosen so a tool need not re-infer it from the (packId, offset) layout; a reader indexes by (z, x, y, t) regardless and does not depend on it. Always a concrete order — never `auto`/`measured`, which resolve at build. Absent on pre-2026-07 archives (writers omit the key rather than emit a default, so pre-field manifests stay byte-identical).

directory.description: Pointer to the single immutable, content-addressed directory object (the v5 run-length index). The object is either a single whole-load buffer (default) or a paged container — root page + leaf pages — selected by `layout`. Either way the leaf codec is v5; `layout`, not `directoryVersion`, discriminates the container shape.

key.description: Object key relative to the dataset root. blake3-128 content address of the at-rest object bytes (the compressed bytes when `encoding` is set).

length.description: Directory object length in bytes — the at-rest object, i.e. the compressed length when `encoding` is set. Readers validate the fetched body against it before any decode.

directoryVersion.description: Directory (leaf) codec version. The packed format emits v5 (per-run pack_id column + object-absolute offsets), wrapped in the 8-byte STTD magic prelude. Unchanged by the paged container.

encoding.description: OPTIONAL at-rest encoding of the directory object. `zstd` = the object is a zstd frame (for a paged directory: EACH page — root + every leaf — is its own zstd frame). Absent = raw codec bytes (the shape of every manifest written before this field existed). Readers MUST support both.

layout.description: OPTIONAL container layout. `paged` = a root page (fixed-width geo-bbox + zoom-range + temporal page descriptors) followed by leaf pages, so a cold reader fetches only the leaves its viewport/time-window touches. Absent or `single` = the whole-load object. Present (with the fields below) iff `paged`.

rootLength.description: Paged only: at-rest byte length of the root page (a prefix of the object). The reader range-GETs `bytes=0-(rootLength-1)` for the root under formatVersion 1, or `bytes=0-(8+rootLength-1)` under formatVersion 2 (the 8-byte STTD object magic shifts the root), then leaf ranges on demand. Leaf descriptor offsets are relative to this (absolute = rootLength + rel_offset, within the post-magic codec bytes).

pageCount.description: Paged only: number of leaf pages (informational / validation).

pageEntries.description: Paged only: nominal entries-per-leaf-page used at build (informational; the sim-validated sweet spot is 1024–4096).

packs.description: Ordered table of immutable, content-addressed pack objects. The index of a pack in this array IS the `pack_id` the directory references. Must be non-empty.

key.description: Object key relative to the dataset root. blake3-128 content address.

length.description: Pack object length in bytes. Normally <= the pack target (64 MiB by default); a single blob larger than the target gets its own oversized pack and may exceed it.

metadata.description: The full stt-core `Metadata` JSON, folded in verbatim (snake_case keys) so a cold reader needs no separate metadata object. Opaque to this schema except for the OPTIONAL `style_hints` block pinned below; see crate::metadata::Metadata.

style_hints.description: OPTIONAL build-time style hints (additive; written by `stt-build --style-hints`). Per-property statistics plus archive-level rendering DEFAULTS a renderer may adopt and a user can always override. Old readers are unaffected — absent means no hints.

version.description: Style-hints block schema version. This schema describes version 1.

properties.description: Per-property statistics. NUMERIC properties carry the percentile fields plus `suggested_domain` (`cardinality` absent); CATEGORICAL (string) properties carry ONLY `name` + `cardinality` — the numeric fields are absent from the JSON, not null-filled.

suggested_domain.description: Suggested render domain `[min, p97]`, each endpoint rounded OUTWARD to 2 significant figures. p97 (not max) encodes the project's manual 'domain clamps at ~p97' tuning convention — a single outlier must not dim the whole ramp (numeric only).

cardinality.description: Distinct-value count (categorical only; the profiler caps it at 10000, so treat the cap value as 'at least this many'). Tolerates `null` for writer flexibility, but the canonical writer omits the key on numeric properties.

suggested_playback_seconds.description: Suggested playback duration in seconds: `clamp(round(sqrt(bucket_count)), 20, 90)` where `bucket_count` = time-range duration / `temporal_bucket_ms`. Absent when the bucket size is unknown/zero.

layer_hint.description: Dominant produced layer kind (absent when none could be derived). Lines with per-vertex times hint `trips`; timeless lines hint `paths`.
